Eastern Michigan Eagles.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide marks the rarity of the tenure instead — in a world where coaches change teams constantly, Chris Creighton is starting a 13th season with the programme.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.dc: Not addressed by name for 2026. The guide records Creighton promoting two defensive assistants rather than hiring outside to replace coordinator Ben Needham.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.dc_status: New — the guide records Ben Needham's departure and two internal promotions, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the unit allowing 6.2 yards per play in each of the last two seasons while generating only 14 sacks.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Noah Kim, a Class of 2020 Michigan State commit now in his seventh season of college football, returning after an 18-to-11 ratio and a MAC-leading 2,817 passing yards, and credits him with enough mobility to evade pressure.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes but is replaced from within. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 13.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator and handled internally, which the guide treats as part of a consistent philosophy — Creighton promoted two defensive assistants rather than hiring outside.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.prior_school: Michigan State is where Noah Kim originally committed. The guide also records Braydon Bennett arriving after averaging over six yards per carry at Coastal Carolina.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.portal_recruiting: A stated contrast read as deliberate philosophy. The guide records the lowest-ranked portal class in the conference per 247Sports but a freshman class tied with Central Michigan for the largest, and reads that as Creighton wanting to build a programme and watch players develop across multiple seasons — admirable and previously successful, but a hard route nowadays.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.vsin_assessment: A philosophy the guide respects and doubts in the same breath. It suspects the Creighton magic may be dwindling, sets the whole case against the era — other programmes appear to be evolving more, and portal success seems paramount now — and interrogates the value of continuity honestly, saying it is unsure how much it matters at Power Four level while suggesting it might matter more in the Group of Six. Its complication is that the defense has more returning production than the offense, and that defense allowed 6.2 yards per play while generating only 14 sacks. It leaves one figure deliberately unresolved: Eastern Michigan went from 5.1 to 5.7 yards per play between 2024 and 2025 yet scored 1.8 fewer points per game.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.strengths: A 13-year head-coaching tenure with unusual continuity, offensive-coordinator and quarterback continuity, the three leading tacklers back, and returning production ranked 24th nationally by Bill Connelly and seventh nationally on Phil Steele's experience chart.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.concerns: The lowest-ranked portal class in the conference in an era the guide says makes portal success paramount, a defense allowing 6.2 yards per play for a second straight season while ranking 131st on third down and 126th in sacks with only nine takeaways, and a less experienced offensive line.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 5.39 wins, with a bowl possible but a ceiling probably of six wins.

Kent State Golden Flashes.previous_hc_experience: Only at Kent State itself. The Coaching Carousel records that starting the season 3-5 meant Mark Carney's interim tag was stripped off, having moved up from offensive coordinator.
Kent State Golden Flashes.oc: Not addressed by name for 2026. Carney himself held the role before the promotion.
Kent State Golden Flashes.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Kent State Golden Flashes.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Kent State Golden Flashes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Kent State Golden Flashes.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Kent State Golden Flashes.defensive_scheme: Not named, but the guide describes a fascinating age split on Cherokee Valeria's defense: portal players who are seniors alongside homegrown talent playing big roles as sophomores, with more explosive plays expected from the transfers now that many are second-year players in the scheme.
Kent State Golden Flashes.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records only 2.9 yards per carry overall and 3.6 in conference games once the brutal non-conference slate is excluded.
Kent State Golden Flashes.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Dru DeShields coming basically out of nowhere for an 18-to-3 ratio with just over 2,000 passing yards, adds the causal note that the redshirt freshman finally kept his ACL intact, and locates the gain in taking care of the football and protecting the quarterback rather than in yardage.
Kent State Golden Flashes.continuity: Head coach and quarterback return; both coordinator positions change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 10.
Kent State Golden Flashes.staff_turnover: Substantial, following Kenni Burns being fired for cause in April and the offensive coordinator moving up. The guide adds Josh Cribbs as the new special teams coordinator and calls him a possible X factor.
Kent State Golden Flashes.portal_recruiting: Addressed as improving. The guide notes the talent level is better again and that a full recruiting cycle for Carney should help, while recording that the receiver room took in few new faces and virtually the entire running back room is new.
Kent State Golden Flashes.vsin_assessment: A turnaround the guide and the Carousel both treat as remarkable. The Coaching Carousel says anybody who wins five games at Kent State deserves Coach of the Year consideration, records the team as 0-16 in MAC play and 1-23 overall under Kenni Burns, calls Carney's .500 conference record and 5-7 season remarkable, notes wins over rival Akron and Bowling Green, and explains the ugly season totals by the 62-14, 66-10 and 44-0 non-conference losses to Texas Tech, Florida State and Oklahoma — concluding Carney's team was competitive most weeks and should be again. The team pages make the same comparison the centrepiece: 0-16 against MAC opponents under Burns, then 4-4 under Carney, with a lot of hope that this was not a one-year blip.
Kent State Golden Flashes.strengths: A head coach who took a 1-23 programme to a .500 conference record, a returning quarterback with an 18-to-3 ratio and a first 20-point-per-game season since 2022, a new special teams coordinator the guide calls a possible X factor, a defense with a sack differential improved from -25 and -29 to -3, and a full recruiting cycle now behind the staff.
Kent State Golden Flashes.concerns: Absolutely no FBS experience behind the starting quarterback, which the guide calls a massive dependency; the top four rushers and top two receivers by yardage gone; 2.9 yards per carry; and a turnover margin still negative despite only three interceptions from the primary quarterback.
Kent State Golden Flashes.betting: The guide's swing game is the finale at Eastern Michigan, an opponent it is very low on. It calls this not a super strong play while noting the talent level is better again and adding Josh Cribbs as a possible X factor, and states it likes the position despite a projection of 3.23 wins.
Kent State Golden Flashes.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens with the standard he thinks applies here: anybody who wins five games at Kent State deserves Coach of the Year consideration. He records the mechanism of the promotion — starting the season 3-5 meant Carney's interim tag was stripped off — and the baseline he inherited: the team was 0-16 in MAC play and 1-23 overall under Kenni Burns, so Carney's .500 record in the conference and 5-7 season was remarkable. He notes they fell short of bowl eligibility but beat rival Akron and also Bowling Green, then explains why the season totals look worse than the team was: losses of 62-14, 66-10 and 44-0 to Texas Tech, Florida State and Oklahoma in non-conference play. Otherwise, he writes, Carney's team was competitive most weeks and should be again this season.

Massachusetts Minutemen.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide, and the guide is explicit about its own uncertainty: it does not even know whether Joe Harasymiak is a good coach.
Massachusetts Minutemen.oc: Max Warner, previously an offensive assistant at Toledo, replacing Mike Bajakian, who left to be the Cleveland Browns' quarterbacks coach.
Massachusetts Minutemen.oc_status: New — the guide records Bajakian's departure and Warner's arrival, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Massachusetts Minutemen.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Massachusetts Minutemen.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Massachusetts Minutemen.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Massachusetts Minutemen.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide raises the possibility that the scheme itself is the cause of the problem, noting the irony that Rutgers — where Harasymiak and Jared Keyte came from — was among the teams with fewer sacks than UMass.
Massachusetts Minutemen.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records UMass rushing for 989 yards total across 12 games.
Massachusetts Minutemen.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide singles out Pop Watson as a possible starter — never really given a chance to start, but a three-star recruit and the MaxPreps High School Quarterback of the Year in Massachusetts in 2021, making this a homecoming — and calls the room much better.
Massachusetts Minutemen.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 8.
Massachusetts Minutemen.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, and the guide's judgement on the departure is unsentimental: with a UMass offense at 3.9 yards per play and an 8-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio from the quarterbacks, Bajakian is not really a big loss, and Warner seems like an upgrade. It notes this is year two for Harasymiak and his assistants otherwise.
Massachusetts Minutemen.prior_school: Rutgers, where Harasymiak and Keyte came from, and which the guide uses ironically against the pass-rush problem. Toledo for Max Warner. On the roster it records Joshua Nobles from Jackson State, William DePaepe from Indiana and Michael Robinson from Rutgers.
Massachusetts Minutemen.portal_recruiting: Improving in quality. The guide counts quite a few Power Four transfers across this portal cycle and the staff's first, and judges the defensive front group decidedly more talented.
Massachusetts Minutemen.vsin_assessment: Unsparing about the season, and openly uncertain about the coach. The guide's summary of 0-12 with 11.1 points per game is a first year to forget, and it measures the programme by its own drought — the last FBS win came against Army on October 8, 2023, in a game where Kay'Ron Lynch-Adams ran for 234 yards, against which it sets the 989 rushing yards across 12 games last season. It diagnoses the season through churn — three different starting quarterbacks, six players with at least 40 rushing attempts, one receiver with 63 catches and nobody else above 27, and 15 players with at least 20 tackles — and reads that as a staff spending essentially the whole season trying to find players who could contribute. Its stated hesitation is that it does not even know whether Harasymiak is a good coach.
Massachusetts Minutemen.strengths: Year two for the head coach and most of his assistants, a defensive coordinator returning, an offensive coordinator the guide calls an upgrade on his predecessor, a quarterback room it calls much better including a homecoming three-star, and quite a few Power Four transfers making the defensive front decidedly more talented.
Massachusetts Minutemen.concerns: An 0-12 season at 11.1 points and 3.9 yards per play, 13 sacks generated with more than five yards per carry allowed and fewer tackles for loss than everyone except Air Force and UCLA, the possibility the guide raises that the scheme itself is the cause, and a season of churn at every position group.
Massachusetts Minutemen.betting: The guide answers its own hardest question — will UMass win a game? — yes, naming Sacred Heart and Stonehill plus home games against Ball State and Eastern Michigan. Its supporting detail is that this is Stonehill's first game against an FBS team, and that Sacred Heart lost by 28 to a UConn team that went 3-9 in 2023, enough to put the Minutemen one win from cashing. Projection is 2.77 wins.

Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Chuck Martin beginning a 13th season in Oxford.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's expectation is a thunder-and-lightning ground game behind an offensive line that played together a lot last season.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide identifies a stout defense as a staple of the Martin era and reads last season generously: 21.7 points allowed was the most since 2022, but the 41 sacks were the most in a long time, and with the offense completing under 50% of its passes the unit faced tougher situations and still allowed under 200 passing yards per game in conference play and just 3.7 yards per carry.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy, but the guide sets a specific target from the programme's own history: 4.94 yards per carry against MAC opponents two seasons ago, against 4.1 last year, which it takes to be the goal for Martin and Pat Welsh.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide narrates a season of upheaval — Brett Gabbert exhausting his eligibility, Dequan Finn quitting before facing his old team, Henry Hesson awful against Toledo, and Thomas Gotkowski finishing as starter at 44.2% — and leans toward Kansas transfer David McComb, arguing he is probably a better fit because he is more Gabbert-like than Finn was.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 9.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator per the Stability Score table.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records David McComb from Kansas, and Caleb Heavner and Rodney Nelson from Division II Fort Hays State.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.portal_recruiting: Addressed at quarterback and running back, drawing twice on the same Division II source in Fort Hays State.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.vsin_assessment: A down year that the guide says went exactly to plan, with the ambition deliberately capped. It argues 7-7 feels like a down year for Martin but that the season actually played out exactly as expected, and caps the ceiling explicitly: even with a Group of Six CFP berth available to someone, it would take something really special for a MAC team to be in the running, so Miami's goals are reasonable and attainable. Its case rests on consistency — 21-6 in MAC play over the last three seasons with at least six wins each time. On the defensive losses it holds both facts: Martin always finds defenders and losing players is nothing new, but it might take some time given who departed.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.strengths: A 13-year head coach with a 21-6 conference record over three seasons and at least six wins each time, defensive-coordinator continuity behind a unit that produced its most sacks in a long time, an offensive line that played together a lot last season, and a quarterback addition the guide considers a better stylistic fit.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.concerns: A new offensive coordinator, a quarterback room that churned through four names last season with the finisher completing 44.2%, a run game at its lowest yards-per-carry since 2022, and extremely heavy defensive losses including three players who amassed more than 300 tackles and a top pass rusher with 8.5 sacks.
Miami (Ohio) RedHawks.betting: With plus money available on eight or more wins, the guide trusts Martin to do what he almost always does. Projection is 7.77 wins.
